correctness.rationale: Independently checked by a velocity-resolvent calculation. With F(v,s)=∫ exp(−rt) E[v_t | v,s, no resets] dt, first-reset conditioning and telegraph relaxation give D=E[vF(v,s)]+r E[vs]F(0,+)/(2λ). The reset age A is exponential and |v|≤aA. Coupling nonlinear and linear zero-start excursions to the same orientation path gives a velocity difference O(t⁴) uniformly (variation of constants and |g(v)−γv|≤C|v|³). On a no-flip excursion it is −κs a³t⁴/4+O(t⁵); the flip event has probability O(t) and therefore changes the expectation only by O(t⁵). Thus the changes in F(0,+) and in E[vs] are −6κa³r⁻⁵+O(r⁻⁶) and −6κa³r⁻⁴+O(r⁻⁵). The same coupling bounds the change in the short-excursion product integrand v₀v_t by C(A+t)⁵, so its discounted integral is O(r⁻⁶). In the long term E[vs]~a/r and F(0,+)~a/r², producing two equal fifth-order contributions. The linear generator gives E[vs]=a/(r+γ+2λ), E[v²]=2aE[vs]/(r+2γ), and D=(E[v²]+aE[vs]/(2λ))/(r+γ). Compactness, odd symmetry and coupling after orientation coalescence and a reset justify the integrable centered covariance. The tan/tanh coefficient and sign follow from their cubic coefficients ±1/3. The result is for fixed λ>0, and fifth order distinguishes drags only if their cubic coefficients differ. The frozen rational checker corroborates a first variation; it is not the proof for arbitrary fixed κ.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The smooth monotone class is narrower but contains the benchmark and examples. For a general admissible law, choose its cubic polynomial on a small interval where its derivative is positive and extend it as a smooth odd strictly increasing drag with an invariant interval. An O(v⁵) drag difference on the common accessible range follows from local agreement and compactness. Coupled excursions then differ by O(t⁶), giving changes O(r⁻⁶) in E[vs], O(r⁻⁷) in F(0,+), and O(r⁻⁸) in the fast product term. Thus the same fingerprint follows by localization; the frozen presentation does not claim an additional distinct physical consequence.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed record states the same fifth-order fingerprint, exact linear reference and tan/tanh comparison under the same reset protocol. The frozen result allows weaker regularity and dissipativity than the indexed theorem, but does not identify a distinct coefficient or a materially new regime: matching the local expansion to a smooth locally monotone reference makes the drag discrepancy O(v⁵), and the same age and resolvent estimates give O(r⁻⁷) in diffusion. The central fingerprint is therefore already covered. This is an assessment of coverage, not an attribution of historical priority based on catalogue dates.
residual_risks: Date paths alone do not establish historical priority, dependence or authorship; the distinct statement-level match drives this review.
The scope does not include a joint limit with λ tending to zero.
